_comment: The texts of Mirror's Edge's README that are its own (tools/title_readme.py has the common ones).
pitch: It starts from a recompilation of the game's executable with ReXGlue v0.10.0, built directly on Any360 from its first day: the sixth title the toolkit runs, and the first on Unreal Engine 3, whose depth pre-pass, predicated tiling and shadow maps fixed renderer bugs every title shares.
own_copy: You need your own copy of the game (the USA disc, title 45410850); the recompiled C++ is generated on your machine from your disc's `default.xex`.

state.recompiled: `default.xex` fully translated (the functions reached only through pointers are declared in [config/](config/))
state.library: not started: the C runtime and XDK functions Any360 already has for the other titles are to be found in this executable and checked in game before they are bound
state.game: not started (the count is in the table above)

run: Both bindings are on by default:

`--any360_gpu=false` draws the game through ReXGlue's GPU instead of `any360::gfx`; `--any360_sys_groups=none` puts the Xbox system calls back on ReXGlue's kernel. `--any360_gpu_occlusion_counts=true` counts the occlusion queries on the GPU (off for now: small models flicker with it).
build: Windows, Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ and Clang tools, an install of the ReXGlue SDK v0.10.0 (`-Sdk`, the folder with `bin\rexglue.exe`, `include\` and `lib\`), an [Any360](https://github.com/GaetanVigner/Any360) checkout (`-Any360`) and FFmpeg's headers for the XMA decoder (`-FFmpeg`).
1. Extract your disc into `game\` (for example with [extract-xiso](https://github.com/XboxDev/extract-xiso)), or make `game\` a junction to it, so that `game\default.xex` exists.
4. Run `out\build\mirrorsedge.exe`. It finds `game\` next to itself or in the repository; logs are written to `out\build\logs\`.

Code reached only through vtables or data pointers is invisible to the codegen: [tools/find-missing-functions.py](tools/find-missing-functions.py) scans the decrypted image (`out\image\default_image.bin`) for such targets and writes them to [config/discovered-functions.toml](config/discovered-functions.toml); the ones only a run of the game reveals are in [config/overrides.toml](config/overrides.toml).
credits: Mirror's Edge by DICE, published by Electronic Arts (2008).
legal: An unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Electronic Arts or DICE. It is not a replacement for the game: you still need to own a copy, and nothing of the game is in this repository.
